review_notes:
I read the whole file, lines 1–230. I did not open external sources because the candidates were all local to the file. I looked for non-trivial reasoning repeated across proofs and found three candidates. I judged all three too small to count under the rubric.

1. `cob_apply_f` and `cob_eq_zero_of_hom` both end in `rw [cob_apply, …, hψ, hψ, Rep.hom_comm_apply …, ← hιeq, map_inv, ρ_ρ_inv, sub_self]`. That is a single rewrite chain of about eight steps. The hypotheses differ: `hψ` holds only on the image of `f` in one lemma and on all of `P` in the other. A shared lemma would need an awkward generalisation to cover both.

2. `mem_cocycles₁_of_forall_κ` and `sub_mem_coboundaries₁` both start with `apply κ_inj κ hκ; intro b; obtain ⟨x, rfl⟩ := hg b` and then `rw [..., κ_ρ π κ hκeq, ← Rep.hom_comm_apply g, ...]`. `cob_of_κ` also uses the `κ_ρ` and `hom_comm_apply g` pair. A helper would only package routine surjectivity and rewriting. It would be a thin wrapper that moves the duplicated branch into a lemma.

3. `toIntLinearMapOfModules` is used three times in `solution`. It is already a shared definition, so nothing is duplicated.

I found no repeated multi-step argument that a shared lemma would clearly improve. The only uncertainty is that I did not try the possible refactors in Lean.
